scams.name: Florida Avenue 'Cambio!' Touts & Counterfeit Peso Exchange
scams.description: Calle Florida is Buenos Aires's main pedestrian shopping street and ground zero for Argentina's informal exchange (cambio) touts — men (arbolitos, 'little trees') who shout '¡Cambio, cambio! Dollar, euro!' at every passing tourist. Community reports document the 2025 pattern after Argentina's Milei-era peso reforms: the historic arbitrage between 'blue dollar' (informal) and official rate has largely collapsed in 2025 — as of late 2025 the blue dollar sometimes trades below the official rate. This means the classic 'get blue dollar from Florida Ave' advice is now often a net loss before fraud even enters the picture. Community reports document the economic inversion. The scam variants: (1) counterfeit peso bills passed as change; (2) bait-and-switch exchange rate (quoted rate drops once you commit); (3) distraction pickpocketing during the transaction; (4) fake 'cueva' (informal exchange office) upstairs that turns out to be a robbery setup. For older travelers in Buenos Aires, the 2025 defensive playbook: (1) refuse all Florida Ave '¡cambio!' approaches — 'No gracias' and keep walking; (2) for USD-to-peso conversion in 2025, Western Union (Plaza San Martín, Retiro branch, and 40+ other city locations) still offers the best rate for cash USD pickups — typically matches or beats blue rate with no counterfeit risk; (3) alternative: download Lemon Cash, Belo, or Ripio apps to receive USDT (stablecoin) and convert to pesos at in-app rates — Legal and competitive; (4) for card payments, most foreign credit cards now automatically apply the MEP/blue-equivalent rate via Argentina's tourist-card scheme (no IVA reimbursement needed) — verify with your card issuer; (5) if you must use an informal cueva, use an established one on the upper floors of Galería Güemes (Florida 165) or similar — never street-level with a stranger; (6) always count bills in daylight and check watermarks + security thread on every note (especially the 1000, 2000, and 10000-peso notes which have the highest counterfeit rate).
scams.avoidance: Refuse all '¡cambio!' street approaches — 'No gracias' + walk Use Western Union for USD-to-peso cash pickup (best 2025 rate) Alternative: Lemon Cash / Belo / Ripio USDT apps for legal crypto conversion Foreign card payments in 2025 auto-apply MEP-equivalent rate — verify with issuer Always count bills in daylight; check watermark + security thread
scams.location: Calle Florida pedestrian street (Microcentro, from Plaza de Mayo to Plaza San Martín), Lavalle pedestrian area, Av. Corrientes at Florida intersection, Galerías Pacífico perimeter

scams.name: Buenos Aires Taxi 'Tacheros Estafadores' — Cloned Meter, Long Route, Short-Change
scams.description: Community reports document Buenos Aires's persistent taxi-driver scam ecosystem through 2025, with travelers describing the pattern in trip-planning posts asking about areas to avoid. Three main variants operate in 2025: (1) Cloned Meter — the meter runs 2–3x legitimate rate; a San Telmo-to-Retiro ride that should cost ~ARS3,500 shows $10,000+ on the meter; drivers target obvious tourists with luggage; (2) Long Route — driver takes a 4–6 km detour ('traffic' excuse) on what should be a direct 2–3 km trip; (3) Counterfeit Return — you hand over a clean 10,000-peso note; driver quickly swaps it for a pre-prepared counterfeit, shows it back to you, claims it was counterfeit, and demands a clean replacement. Variant (4): floating tariff — driver has 'just changed tariff' mid-ride without authorization; refuses printed receipt. Variant (5): credit-card 'broken' — POS terminal 'fails' so you must pay cash, at which point counterfeit-return or rounded-up-cash scam runs. For older travelers in Buenos Aires, the 2025 defensive playbook: (1) use Uber, Cabify, or DiDi exclusively — all three operate legally in BA and bypass every taxi scam variant; fares are transparent and app-paid (no cash handling); Uber/Cabify from San Telmo to Recoleta runs ~$2,500–$4,000 ARS in 2025; (2) if you must take a street taxi, use only clearly-marked 'Radio Taxi' cars (yellow-and-black with roof light) — never unmarked or 'remis' flagged down on the street; (3) insist the meter starts at the base tariff (ARS260 in 2025, check sign on dashboard); watch it count up; (4) pay with small bills matched closely to the fare ($100 / $500 / $1,000 denominations) — never hand over a 10,000 or 20,000 peso note; (5) demand the printed receipt (recibo) and the driver's name/número; legitimate drivers always provide both; (6) for airport runs, use Manuel Tienda León shared-shuttle bus (ARS15,000), Tienda León private taxi ($35,000), or Uber — avoid Terminal-A 'Remis' touts.
scams.avoidance: Use Uber / Cabify / DiDi exclusively — all legal, transparent fares in BA If street taxi: Radio Taxi only (yellow-and-black + roof light) Pay in small bills ($500/$1,000) matched to the fare — never $10,000+ Demand printed recibo + driver's name/número Airport: Manuel Tienda León shuttle ($15k) or Tienda León taxi ($35k)
scams.location: San Telmo, La Boca, Retiro, Microcentro (around Florida Ave), Palermo Soho nightlife zones, airport transfer runs, late-night from bars/restaurants

scams.name: Bird Poop / Mustard Distraction Pickpocket
scams.description: Community reports document Buenos Aires's most effective distraction-pickpocket operation, with one 2025 solo traveler writing about falling for the scam; the canonical Southern-Cone variant has been documented since at least 2016 in Santiago. The setup runs in 3 phases: (1) a confederate squirts a liquid (mustard, ketchup, chocolate syrup, or actual bird-droppings simulant) onto the victim's back or shoulder from above or behind; (2) a second team member appears with napkins, offering to 'help clean' — they pat the victim down enthusiastically; (3) during the patting, a third team member lifts wallet, phone, or passport from an unzipped bag or back pocket. Peak-activity zones in Buenos Aires: Plaza de Mayo during weekday business hours, Caminito's narrow cobblestone streets, Recoleta Cemetery entrance queue, San Telmo Feria de Pedro crowded aisles, and Puerto Madero dinner-hour foot traffic. The scam often targets 55+ travelers because of slower reaction time and higher-value items (watches, camera gear). For older travelers in Buenos Aires, the defensive playbook: (1) if you feel anything hit your back/shoulder unexpectedly, do not stop — walk briskly to a shop entrance, cafe, or hotel lobby and check yourself in their bathroom mirror; (2) refuse all 'cleaning help' from strangers, no matter how apologetic or insistent they seem; the 'good Samaritan' is part of the team; (3) keep wallet in a front pocket or money belt under clothing — never in a back pocket or bag top; (4) keep phone + passport in separate locations (e.g., passport in hotel safe + phone in zipped bag + wallet in money belt) so one loss doesn't cascade; (5) in Caminito, Recoleta, and San Telmo peak hours, wear a small crossbody bag in front of your body with one hand on the strap; (6) if you're hit while alone with no nearby business, call '911' (BA emergency) or walk to the nearest cafe and use their bathroom; (7) report theft to the Comisaría Turística (Tourist Police, Av. Corrientes 436, +54 11 4346 5748, 24/7 English service) within 24h — Required for travel insurance claims.
scams.avoidance: If something hits your back: walk briskly to a cafe/shop — Do NOT stop on the street Refuse all 'cleaning help' from strangers — the 'helper' is part of the team Wallet in front pocket or money belt; never back pocket or bag top Passport + cash in separate locations (hotel safe vs money belt) Report theft: Comisaría Turística Av. Corrientes 436, +54 11 4346 5748
scams.location: Plaza de Mayo, Puerto Madero riverfront walk, Avenida 9 de Julio crossings, Recoleta Cemetery perimeter, La Boca/Caminito tourist strip, San Telmo Sunday market (Feria de San Pedro Telmo)

scams.name: EZE / AEP Airport 'Remis' Overcharge & Meet-Greet Service Scam
scams.description: Community reports document Buenos Aires airport-transfer scams and overlapping taxi-driver estafador patterns throughout 2025. EZE (Ezeiza) is 35 km from central Buenos Aires (45–60 min drive); AEP (Aeroparque) is 3 km from central BA (15–20 min). Legitimate 2025 options: (1) Manuel Tienda León shared bus from EZE to Retiro (downtown BA) — ARS15,000 one-way, departs every 30 min, scam-proof; (2) Manuel Tienda León private taxi at the official counter — $35,000–$45,000 ARS flat to most central addresses; (3) Uber/Cabify via app from EZE designated rideshare zone — typically $25,000–$40,000 ARS depending on surge; (4) from AEP, Uber/Cabify $6,000–$12,000 ARS to central BA. Scam variants: (1) 'Remis' touts in Terminal-A arrivals hall quoting $80,000–$150,000 ARS ('flat rate' 3–4x legitimate); (2) 'Private Meet & Greet Service' websites demanding USD prepayment at $80–$150 USD for what costs ARS35,000 ($35 USD) via Tienda León; (3) driver claims 'meter broken' then demands cash in USD; (4) driver takes indirect route via Autopista Ricchieri (adds 30% distance); (5) 'shared shuttle' tout charging per-person at ARS20,000 × 4 passengers when Tienda León bus is $15,000 one-way total. For older travelers arriving at EZE or AEP in 2025, the clean playbook: (1) walk past all 'Remis' and 'Meet & Greet' touts in the arrivals hall — they're unlicensed and overcharge; (2) proceed to the official Manuel Tienda León counter (clearly marked 'Tienda León' signage inside the terminal) for bus or taxi tickets — $15k/$35k respectively; (3) for Uber/Cabify/DiDi, walk to the designated rideshare pickup zone (EZE: 'Parking de Ride Sharing' signs outside Terminal A) and request via app — use WiFi in the arrivals hall to confirm fare screenshot before walking out; (4) if you prefer pre-booked, use Viator, GetYourGuide, or your hotel concierge (verified operators) — expect to pay $45–$60 USD for EZE-to-central-BA private; (5) refuse pre-booking via unfamiliar 'Meet & Greet' websites demanding USD prepayment; (6) always confirm the driver's license plate matches the app screenshot; photograph the plate before entering the car; (7) pay via app (Uber/Cabify/DiDi) or card at Tienda León — avoid cash payment at the end of the ride.
scams.avoidance: Walk past all arrivals-hall 'Remis' / 'Meet & Greet' touts Manuel Tienda León bus $15k ARS to Retiro — buy at official counter inside terminal Tienda León private taxi $35k–$45k ARS at same counter Uber/Cabify/DiDi from designated rideshare zone with app fare screenshot Pay via app or card at Tienda León — avoid cash at end of ride
scams.location: Ezeiza International Airport (EZE) Terminal A + B arrivals hall, Aeroparque Jorge Newbery (AEP) arrivals curb, Retiro bus terminal pickup zone, 'Meet & Greet' and 'Private Transfer' online booking sites

scams.name: Counterfeit Peso Bills Returned as Change
scams.description: Community reports frame the counterfeit-peso pattern, which remains active in Argentina throughout 2025. Argentina's high-denomination bills (1000, 2000, 10000 pesos; 20000 note introduced 2024) have elevated counterfeit rates — particularly the 1000 and 2000 notes. The primary scam vectors: (1) unofficial 'cambio' / 'cueva' exchange returns a stack with 1–3 counterfeit bills mixed in; (2) taxi driver performs bill-switch — you hand over a clean note, driver shows you a counterfeit and demands a real replacement; (3) small-shop clerk gives change with counterfeits after you pay with a large denomination; (4) street-vendor 'Mercado Pago' QR scam where the scan shows a payment that was reversed; (5) ATMs at small independent operators (not Banco Nación, Santander, BBVA, HSBC, or Galicia main branches) occasionally dispense counterfeit. For older travelers in Buenos Aires in 2025, the defensive playbook: (1) know the security features: genuine 1000-peso note (General Juan Manuel de Rosas) has a 3D-effect security thread, watermark of Rosas's face, and color-shifting '1000' in lower right corner; genuine 2000-peso note (Ramón Carrillo + Cecilia Grierson) has a color-shifting '2000' and tactile relief; (2) always count exchange and change in daylight or strong artificial light — Hold each high-denomination bill up to the light to check watermark; (3) if a bill feels 'flat' or 'papery' rather than having the tactile relief of genuine pesos, it's counterfeit — Real pesos have raised ink you can feel; (4) use cards (Visa/Mastercard) for any transaction over ARS50,000 — Virtually eliminates counterfeit-return risk; (5) use ATMs only at Banco Nación, Santander Río, BBVA, HSBC, Galicia, or Macro main branches — Not at street-level small ATMs in pharmacies or mini-markets; (6) for taxi payment, match bills as close as possible to the fare — ARS3,500 ride should be paid with $3,500 or $4,000 in small bills, not a $10,000 bill; (7) if you receive suspected counterfeit, report to the Banco Central (BCRA) hotline at 0800-999-6663 and the Comisaría Turística.
scams.avoidance: Count all exchange + change in daylight — Hold up to light for watermark Feel for tactile relief on genuine pesos (raised ink on portrait + numerals) Use Visa/Mastercard for transactions over ARS50,000 ATMs: Banco Nación / Santander / BBVA / HSBC / Galicia / Macro main branches only Pay taxis with small bills ($500/$1,000) matched to fare — never $10,000+
scams.location: Informal 'cueva' exchange houses, Florida Ave cambio touts, street-vendor transactions at San Telmo Sunday market, late-night taxi payments, small shops in tourist zones

scams.name: Buenos Aires Airbnb / Temporary Rental Off-Platform & 'Illegal Cash' Fraud
scams.description: Community reports document the 2025 Buenos Aires-specific Airbnb fraud pattern, including a traveler who booked a month-long Buenos Aires Airbnb and couldn't check in, alongside broader platform-level reports on Buenos Aires 'cash-only' TOS-violation fraud. Argentina's long-term rental market (mes por mes, 'month by month') traditionally priced in USD cash due to peso instability, and Milei-era reforms haven't fully changed the informal-cash culture by 2025. Common scam patterns: (1) Airbnb host requests the stay be 'paid partly via Airbnb, partly in USD cash on arrival' to 'avoid Argentina taxes' — this violates Airbnb TOS and leaves the guest with zero protection on the cash portion; if anything goes wrong, Airbnb support treats the reservation as fraudulent; (2) off-platform WhatsApp 'Buenos Aires long-term rental' listings demanding USD cash on arrival + 'deposit' — property is often fake, host disappears; (3) Facebook Marketplace 'Palermo apartment' at 30% below market rate with Zelle/PayPal/crypto demand; (4) legitimate-seeming 'host' photos stolen from real Airbnb listings; (5) in-person viewing where 'landlord' shows the apartment then disappears after cash hand-off. For older travelers booking Buenos Aires accommodation, the protective playbook: (1) book short-term stays only through Airbnb, VRBO, or Booking.com platform payment in full — never accept 'partly cash on arrival' requests, regardless of what the host says about Argentina taxes (it's a TOS violation and invalidates your protection); (2) for long-term stays (1+ month), use ZonaProp, ArgenProp, or Remax Argentina (the three legitimate local real-estate portals) — never WhatsApp or Facebook Marketplace listings; (3) for USD-cash-required legitimate rentals, require a signed Spanish-language contract (contrato de alquiler temporario) with the landlord's DNI (national ID) + property escritura (title) information; (4) pay any USD cash via Western Union transfer (generates a paper trail) rather than hand-to-hand; (5) legitimate Buenos Aires hotels and serviced apartments: Alvear Palace Hotel (Recoleta), Palacio Duhau - Park Hyatt, Faena Hotel (Puerto Madero), NH Collection Buenos Aires Jousten, Hotel Madero; (6) avoid Palermo / Recoleta 'luxury apartment' ads at <50% of comparable verified listings — Too-good-to-be-true is the tell; (7) report fraud to the Defensa del Consumidor (consumer protection, 0800-666-1518) and to the Comisaría Turística.
scams.avoidance: Book STRs only through Airbnb / VRBO / Booking.com platform payment in full Long-term rentals: ZonaProp / ArgenProp / Remax Argentina only — never WhatsApp If USD cash is legally required: signed Spanish contract + landlord DNI + property escritura Pay USD cash via Western Union (paper trail) — never hand-to-hand Report fraud: Defensa del Consumidor 0800-666-1518 + Comisaría Turística
scams.location: Palermo Soho / Hollywood short-term rentals, Recoleta luxury apartment STRs, San Telmo historic-building apartments, off-platform WhatsApp / Facebook Marketplace listings
